paragraphs.source_en: The final six chapters of this book narrate the period from 1789 to 1922, the last 133 years of the Ottoman dynasty and empire. This era was marked by diverse attempts by administrators, intellectuals, sultans, and military leaders to save the empire from its own worst tendencies and dismemberment by foreign powers. As the Ottomans became ever more connected to the rest of Europe, for good and for ill, they sought to hold the empire together in the face of internal rebellion and revolution. They grasped for new ways to link the dynasty to its subjects, experimenting with ever more radical and modern forms of governance, war, and violence.
